headline_summary: The clearest architecture wins came from partial RoPE and partial key offset (PKO), cached attention, block attention residuals, and their combined recipe. The combined recipe reached 1.21–1.52x measured effective speedup across four scales. MuonH improved measured speed by 1.19–1.33x, but its four-point fit was slightly worse at the longest projection. Router modifications were mostly negative: frozen and nonlinear routers failed, while restricting router z-loss to selected or non-selected experts was promising but only tested at two scales.

title: Partial key offset
summary: Both placements passed gate 2. The every-fourth-layer variant projected better; measured speedups were about 1.07–1.20x.

title: Partial RoPE
summary: Rotating half the head dimensions improved macro loss with negligible throughput cost, giving about 1.09–1.12x at gate 1 and a gate-2 pass.

title: PKO plus partial RoPE
summary: The two changes were additive: 1.09–1.23x across four scales, with better projected loss at `1e21` and `1e23` FLOPs.

title: PKO plus partial RoPE on the last layer
summary: Forcing the last layer to use long attention and PKO raised the family to 1.19–1.23x across four scales.

title: MHA plus PKO
summary: MHA and PKO remained complementary without GQA, reaching 1.28–1.37x at gate 1.

title: Paired-head attention
summary: A gate-1 sweep was submitted, but the issue records no usable result.

title: Inkling relative position
summary: The corrected d512 QK-scale arm ended 13.5% worse in Paloma BPB with no throughput win; d768 also ran about 24% below baseline throughput.

title: Value embeddings
summary: One initialization was neutral and the other split by scale; a 3–5% throughput and activation-memory cost erased the quality gain.

title: Wide attention
summary: More heads consistently improved quality enough to cover a 5–8% throughput cost, but the gate-2 win was marginal at 1.04–1.07x.

title: MHA instead of GQA
summary: MHA passed gate 2 at 1.10–1.18x. The recipe kept GQA anyway to retain a 4x smaller KV cache.

title: RoPE before QK norm
summary: Reordering RoPE and QK normalization was empirically neutral at both gate-1 scales.

title: QK multiplier sweep
summary: Neither 1.1 nor 1.5 beat the default consistently across scales; both failed the full gate.

title: Remove QK norm and multiplier
summary: The variant improved only d768 and fell below 1x at d512, d1024, and d1280. QK norm stayed in the recipe.

title: Learnable per-head QK gain
summary: Full-projection normalization plus a per-layer gain reached 1.086x at d512 and 1.054x at d768, but no larger-scale runs anchored the trend.

title: QK gated norm
summary: Key gating won at d512 while query gating won at d768. The scale inversion and missing larger cells prevented a recipe choice.

title: Finer expert granularity
summary: Doubling active and total experts improved loss slightly but cut throughput by roughly 30%, producing 0.72–0.76x speedup.

title: Slim layers
summary: Replacing the first MoE layer was nearly loss-neutral and reached 1.059x at d768; most individual layers could be slimmed profitably, but a full recipe was not tested.

title: 256 routed experts
summary: E256 improved with scale, reaching 1.17x at d768 and 1.252x at d1024, but missed at d512 and OOMed at d1280.

title: Routed output scale and expert LR
summary: Closed without measurements after the planned sweep was superseded.

title: Null experts
summary: Null experts recovered some of the cost of picking five experts, but all tested variants remained below the simpler pick-four baseline.

title: Pick five with a smaller shared expert
summary: Rebalancing shared and routed capacity made pick-five viable, but speedup moved from 1.011x at d512 to 0.993x at d768.

title: Alternating dense and MoE blocks
summary: The open issue contains no usable experimental comparison yet.

title: Nonzero router-bias initialization
summary: The tested initializations were neutral and failed gate 1.

title: Router combine activation
summary: Moving the sigmoid before QB selection was catastrophically worse; compressing logits before bias selection broke routing.

title: Minimum expert combine weight
summary: Floors hurt throughout the standard recipe; the only small no-z-loss gain at d512 vanished by d768.

title: Sqrt-softplus combine weights
summary: All four z-loss variants were slower than baseline at 0.97–0.99x.

title: Selected versus non-selected router z-loss
summary: All four cells beat baseline at 1.015–1.036x. The selected-only form was scale-stable, but no d1024 or d1280 run confirmed it.

title: Router orthogonality loss
summary: Best cells reached 1.016x and 1.009x, but the optimal coefficient moved by two orders of magnitude between scales.

title: Frozen router
summary: Freezing random routing produced a 35–40% effective slowdown, showing that learned routing directions matter.

title: MLP router
summary: The nonlinear router reached only 0.975x and 0.936x; the linear router was already the better model.

title: Frozen router with learnable expert scales
summary: Per-expert scales did not recover the frozen-router penalty; all variants stayed near 0.55–0.66x.

title: Muon AOL coefficients
summary: The initial Muon comparison was superseded by the MuonH path before a final metric table was recorded.

title: MuonH with a 2x-batch ablation
summary: The first run exposed and fixed an optimizer-sharding bug; the line continued with MuonH, but this issue does not contain a clean final comparison.

title: MuonH heuristic, AdamH 2x, and Muon search
summary: Tuned plain Muon barely won at d512 and lost at d768; AdamH 2x lost at both. MuonH remained the follow-up direction.

title: GrugMuon on expert MLPs
summary: The best cells reached 1.071x and 1.108x, but the experiment changed both optimizer and expert topology, so the source of the gain is unresolved.

title: Nano walks: Muon versus AdamH
summary: Muon fit the Nemotron training distribution better, while AdamH was better on out-of-distribution Paloma, especially code.

title: MuonH matrix optimizer
summary: MuonH delivered 1.19–1.33x across the four measured scales, but its slightly shallower fit tied near `1e21` and projected 0.011 worse at `1e23`.

title: MuonH magnitude-direction decoupling
summary: Loss improved at both gate-1 scales, but roughly 6.5% throughput overhead kept the best first-pass speedup just below 1x.

title: Newton–Schulz coefficient ablation
summary: The open issue has no recorded result yet.

title: Bfloat16 Newton–Schulz
summary: The experiment is set up to isolate bandwidth savings inside Newton–Schulz; no final two-scale verdict is recorded.

title: Depth-MuP LR sensitivity
summary: Small-scale evidence is split: about 0.963x at d512 and 1.040x at d768. Larger-scale LR optima are still being resolved.

title: AdamH embedding initialization
summary: Initializing embeddings at standard deviation 1.0 passed all four scales; the gain declined from about 5% to 1.4% but stayed positive.

title: Gradient clipping sweep
summary: Clip values 0.1 and 0.3 marginally passed gate 1, with up to 1.045x, but the gain was too small to justify gate 2.

title: AdamH on the attention gate
summary: Moving the attention gate into AdamH failed gate 1.

title: AdamH epsilon sweep
summary: Every alternative failed gate 1; `1e-4` was especially poor and the existing scaled epsilon remained best.

title: Gradient-aware hyperball
summary: Both forward-normalization variants were worse at both gate-1 scales.

title: Delayed-gradient pipeline parallelism
summary: Per-stage staleness was much cheaper than a global delay, and the modeled DCN-bound regime reached 1.08–1.73x net speedup; real pipeline-parallel validation remains open.

title: Bfloat16 master precision
summary: The remaining loss gap came from low-LR cooldown updates, and bfloat16 master weights provided no throughput or MFU gain on v4-32.

title: X0 skip connections
summary: The variant stayed above 1x at all four measured scales, but its gain shrank from 1.120x to 1.043x and its long-range projections were slightly worse.

title: Layer-grain prediction
summary: Improvements were at most 0.005 macro loss and vanished at d1024; projected benefit was below 0.001.

title: Pseudogram residual
summary: The per-position sigmoid residual failed gate 1.

title: Backout residual
summary: Subtracting a cached midpoint activation failed gate 1.

title: Cached attention
summary: Reusing the attention input in the last three layers was effectively free and reached 1.02–1.10x across four scales.

title: Block attention residuals
summary: Grouping representations in blocks of four passed gate 2 at 1.06–1.12x despite a 4–7% throughput cost.

title: Full attention residuals
summary: Giving every sub-operation its own residual entry improved loss but cost 9–14% throughput; the block form was better.

title: Identity Hyper-Connections
summary: The open issue has a completed gate-1 pass: 1.0515x at d512 and 1.0205x at d768 after charging 7–10% throughput overhead.

title: Depth-width shift
summary: Removing one layer raised throughput about 10% and passed both small scales, but it requires a new isoflop and LR fit before adoption.

title: Barebones transformer
summary: Removing MoE routing, GatedNorm, and XSA cost roughly 0.10–0.14 macro loss with AdamH; the existing components were collectively useful.

title: Deeper networks
summary: Deeper shapes were consistently 0.009–0.021 worse than the baseline scaling prediction at their best learning rates.

title: Gated post-norm
summary: The extra post-sublayer RMSNorm and gate worsened d512 loss and cut throughput about 4%, yielding 0.906x.

title: Remove logit z-loss
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: Removal was neutral at gate 1 but regressed at d1024 and d1280, so logit z-loss stayed as a stabilizer.

title: Split router and shared-expert norms
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: Separate norms did not improve quality; the shared MLP norm was sufficient for all paths.

title: LM-head initialization scale
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: Neither 2x nor 4x passed the four-scale gate. The apparent d768 gain at 4x did not repeat.

title: LM-head softcap
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: Loss-only speedup exceeded 1x at all four points, but wall-clock cost and a worse scaling-law projection failed the strict promotion rule.

title: Embedding ablations
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: Most equal-throughput variants have finished, but one d768 cell crashed and the remaining MLP-without-RMS arm was still running.

title: GEGLU
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: GEGLU marginally passed both small scales at roughly 1–2%, but its 2% throughput cost left too little gain for gate 2.

title: Double SwiGLU
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: The result inverted from 0.972x at d512 to 1.056x at d768, with no larger-scale tie-breaker.

title: RMSNorm before the SwiGLU swish
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: The parameter-free norm was loss-neutral at about 0.5% throughput cost. It achieved scale invariance, but not a compute speedup.

title: SiTU
category: Activations, normalization, embeddings, and output head
summary: SiTU regressed quality with flat throughput, reaching only 0.76x at d512 and 0.72x at d768.

title: FineWeb-Edu baseline plus PKO
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: PKO generalized beyond the Nemotron mix: macro loss improved by 0.056 at d512 and 0.048 at d768 with flat or better throughput.

title: Position-weighted loss
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: Downweighting early document tokens improved training loss but not Paloma or Uncheatable evals; d512 was about 2% slower and d768 did not finish.

title: Sequence-length sweep
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: None of 1k, 2k, or 8k beat the 4k baseline at both scales; 4k remained the best tradeoff.

title: Chunked inference throughput
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: Early results suggested better 32k prefill with similar decode, but the active repeated-timing matrix superseded those measurements.

title: Focus crawl versus general crawl
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: At d512 and d768, the focus crawl won on arXiv and S2ORC while the general crawl won on broad web, news, and Paloma macro; larger cells remain open.

title: MRCR context perplexity
category: Training setup, data, objective, serving, and evaluation
summary: Retaining up to 8,192 tokens of context cut final-turn perplexity from 21.09 to 10.40, a 2.03x ratio, across the 2-, 4-, and 8-needle subsets.

title: Combined-best recipe
summary: E128, PKO, partial RoPE, last-layer PKO, and cached attention combined nearly additively, reaching 1.21–1.52x across four scales.

title: May architecture synthesis
summary: The combined recipe beat baseline at three tested widths, but the isoflop sweep showed pick-four E256 dominated the proposed pick-six form; the synthesis changed the final configuration.

title: AdamH on token embeddings
summary: Moved token embeddings to AdamH and feeds the May architecture.

title: k6e256s5 expert configuration
summary: Introduced the `k6e256s5` expert configuration used in #5371.

title: May architecture plus MuonH
summary: Defined the MuonH May recipe used as the baseline for #5938.

title: July baseline
summary: Defined the July baseline used by #7208 and #7255.
